title: Nursing Career Towards Financial Independence
authors: Mary Grace B. Nduka, Michael B. Benedicto
tldr: A qualitative phenomenological study exploring how 28 Filipino nurses from Metro Manila government hospitals perceive nursing as a pathway to financial independence, identifying seven themes and proposing the N-FERP framework for nurse financial empowerment.
problem_and_motivation: Despite heavy outmigration of Filipino nurses seeking higher pay abroad, there is limited research on the financial experiences of nurses who remain in the Philippines. Understanding how nursing careers help or hinder financial independence is critical for workforce retention policy.
approach: Qualitative phenomenological design using Colaizzi's method of data analysis
Purposive sampling of 28 Registered Nurses from 3 government hospitals in Metro Manila
Semi-structured in-depth interviews and focus group discussions
Data analysis through seven procedural steps: collection, extraction, formulation of meanings, theme clustering, integration, member checking, and validation
Demographic profiling to understand participant backgrounds (age, sex, civil status, educational attainment, number of dependents)
Thematic analysis to identify patterns in financial experiences
Proposal of N-FERP (Nurse Financial Empowerment and Resilience Program) framework
findings: cat: Majority were female (64.29%), aged 33-39 (53.57%), married (57.14%), with master's degrees (53.57%).
cat: 89.29% were family breadwinners; 53.57% supported 4 or more dependents beyond themselves.
cat: Job positions ranged from Nurse I to Nurse V with salary grades from SG-2 to SG-6 (50%).
cat: Seven emergent themes identified: Personal Security, Professional Motivation, Family Support, Career Development, Stress Reduction, Autonomy, and Retirement.
qlt: Single nurses living alone can cover basic needs but cannot accumulate savings.
qlt: Single nurses acting as breadwinners face substantial financial strain.
qlt: Married nurses share financial responsibilities but face challenges with large family sizes.

qlt: N-FERP proposed as a five-component program: Financial Literacy Training, Structured Savings and Investment Programs, Career Advancement Support, Mental Health and Wellness Support, and Policy Advocacy and Workplace Reforms.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Provides a nuanced qualitative understanding of how Filipino government hospital nurses experience financial (in)dependence within the nursing career, highlighting the tension between professional fulfillment and financial strain, and proposing a multi-component intervention framework.
directly_justifies: Odin's user studies on financial behavior should account for career-related and cultural factors like breadwinner culture.
Qualitative research methods complement quantitative financial modeling in understanding user needs.
Financial independence concerns vary significantly by career stage, marital status, and family obligations.
limits: Limited to 28 participants from only 3 hospitals in Metro Manila; not generalizable to all Philippine nurses.
Qualitative methodology does not include quantitative financial metrics or causal analysis.
N-FERP proposed but not implemented or evaluated.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Non-algorithmic Philippine study on career financial experiences, covering financial literacy, employment, career development, workplace context, and socioeconomic impact.

limitations: Small sample size of 28 nurses from only three government hospitals in Metro Manila.
Qualitative, phenomenological design limits generalizability and does not provide statistical or causal evidence.
Potential social desirability bias in self-reported financial experiences during interviews.
N-FERP remains a proposed framework with no implementation or outcome evaluation.
Findings specific to Philippine public hospital context; not generalizable to private hospitals or other countries.
remember_this: 89.29% of Filipino government nurses are family breadwinners; 53.57% support 4+ dependents.
Seven themes: Personal Security, Professional Motivation, Family Support, Career Development, Stress Reduction, Autonomy, Retirement.
Single nurses living alone cover basic needs but cannot save; single breadwinner nurses face severe financial strain.
N-FERP proposed: Financial Literacy Training, Savings Programs, Career Support, Mental Health, Policy Advocacy.
